landmarks.name: Iguazu Falls
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest and most spectacular waterfall systems in the world, located on the border with Brazil.

wiki.extract:
Puerto Iguazú is a border city in the province of Misiones, Argentina. With a population of 82,227 ,
it is the fourth largest city in the Province, after Posadas, Oberá, and Eldorado.
The Iguazú Falls are 18 kilometres (11 mi) away from the city, and as a result the city has developed much of its infrastructure around tourism.

landmarks.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
landmarks.writeup: A massive glacier in Patagonia known for its dynamic ice ruptures and stunning blue ice formations.

wiki.extract: The Perito Moreno, Francisco Gormaz or Bismarck Glacier is a glacier located in Los Glaciares National Park in southwest Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, and originated in the Magallanes Region in Chile, being also part of the Bernardo O'Higgins National Park. It is one of the most important tourist attractions in the Argentine Patagonia.

landmarks.name: Casa Rosada
landmarks.writeup: The executive mansion and office of the President of Argentina, located in Buenos Aires.

wiki.extract: The Casa Rosada, lit. 'the pink house', is the president of the Argentine Republic's official workplace, located in Buenos Aires. The palatial mansion is known officially as Casa de Gobierno. Normally, the president lives at the Quinta de Olivos, the president of Argentina's official residence, located in Olivos, Greater Buenos Aires. The characteristic color of the Casa Rosada is baby pink, and it is considered one of the most emblematic buildings in Buenos Aires. The building also houses a museum, which contains objects relating to former presidents of Argentina. It has been declared a National Historic Monument of Argentina.

landmarks.name: La Boca
landmarks.writeup: A colorful neighborhood in Buenos Aires famous for its vibrant street art and tango culture.

wiki.extract: La Boca is a neighborhood (barrio) of Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina.

landmarks.name: Aconcagua
landmarks.writeup: The highest mountain in the Americas, located in the Andes mountain range.

wiki.extract: Aconcagua is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina. With a summit elevation of 6,967.15 metres, it is the highest mountain in the Americas, the highest outside Asia, and the highest peak in both the Western and Southern Hemispheres. It is the second-most topographically prominent peak in the world and one of the Seven Summits, the highest mountains on each of the seven continents.

cultural_events.name: Carnaval
cultural_events.writeup: A lively festival celebrated with parades, music, and dancing, especially vibrant in the northern provinces.

wiki.extract: Carnival is a festive season at the close of the Christian pre-Lenten period, consisting of Quinquagesima or Shrove Sunday, Shrove Monday, and Shrove Tuesday or Mardi Gras.

cultural_events.name: Tango Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event in Buenos Aires celebrating the traditional Argentine dance and music.

wiki.extract: Argentine tango is a musical genre and accompanying social dance originating at the end of the 19th century in the suburbs of Buenos Aires. It typically has a 24 or 44 rhythmic time signature, and two or three parts repeating in patterns such as ABAB or ABCAC. Its lyrics are marked by nostalgia, sadness, and laments for lost love. The typical orchestra has several melodic instruments and is given a distinctive air by the bandoneon. It has continued to grow in popularity and spread internationally, adding modern elements without replacing the older ones. Among its leading figures are the singer and songwriter Carlos Gardel and composers/performers Francisco Canaro, Juan D'Arienzo, Carlos Di Sarli, Osvaldo Pugliese, Elvira Santamaría, and Ástor Piazzolla.

cultural_events.name: Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia
cultural_events.writeup: The National Grape Harvest Festival held in Mendoza, celebrating the wine harvest with parades and performances.

wiki.extract: Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia takes place annually in Mendoza City, Argentina. It is one of the most important festivals in the country, attracting large numbers of tourists to the region. It is a celebration of wine and the winemaking industry.

food_writeup: Argentine cuisine is renowned for its beef, particularly asado (barbecue), empanadas, and mate, a traditional herbal tea. Italian and Spanish influences are prominent in the culinary landscape.
brief_history: Argentina declared independence from Spain in 1816. It experienced periods of economic growth and political instability throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, including military dictatorships and democratic transitions. Today, it is a federal republic with a diverse cultural heritage.

important_people.name: Eva Perón
important_people.description: Influential political figure and First Lady

current_conflicts: Argentina has no active armed conflicts but faces ongoing economic challenges and territorial disputes, notably over the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas) with the United Kingdom.
